These guides back the two assessed deliverables — the midterm report (40%) and the final paper (60%) — from picking a topic through to the write-up. They treat both as submissions to ACL / EMNLP / NAACL / COLM / ICLR rather than as coursework, which is the standard the course is aiming at.

**The guides themselves are in Chinese**, matching how the course is taught; the report template is in English, like the papers you will write.

| Guide | What it covers |
|:-------------------------------|:--------------------------|
| **[Problem Cards for an ACL 2027 Paper](supplements/topics-for-acl27.qmd)**<br>[選題問題卡：寫一篇 ACL 論文的起點]{.wk-zh} | 25 problem cards on Taiwan's languages, tokenization, long context and efficiency, training and alignment, retrieval and agents, and evaluation. Each gives the pain point, the evidence to collect first, resources checked against official pages on 2026-10-16, open directions, risks, and the kind of contribution; the method is left to you. |
| **[Midterm: From Problem Statement to Proof of Concept](supplements/midterm-poc.qmd)**<br>[期中研究計畫與概念驗證（PoC）教戰守策：從問題定義到初期驗證]{.wk-zh} | How to frame a falsifiable hypothesis and position it against prior art, the fatal flaws reviewers look for first, and where AI tools belong in the process. |
| **[Final Paper: From PoC to a Conference-Ready Manuscript](supplements/final-paper-mvp.qmd)**<br>[期末完整論文（MVP）教戰守策：從 PoC 跨越至 Top Conference 錄取門檻]{.wk-zh} | The section-by-section structure, the experiments that establish soundness, the qualitative error analysis reviewers actually read, and a rubric aligned with ARR's scoring dimensions. |
| **[Writing and Narrative Logic for Top-Conference Papers](supplements/paper-writing-and-narrative.qmd)**<br>[Top Conference 論文寫作教戰守策：敘事架構、工程實踐與 AI 協同]{.wk-zh} | The narrative arc of a top-conference paper, sentence-level coherence tactics, an AI-assisted writing workflow, and a reviewer's-eye checklist before submission. |
| **[Report Template: Midterm Report and Final Paper](supplements/report-template.qmd)**<br>[期中報告與期末論文的 LaTeX 範本（ARR long paper）]{.wk-zh} | The LaTeX project for both reports, in ACL Rolling Review long-paper format, with guidance written from an ARR reviewer's point of view. Download the ZIP and import it into Prism. |

> **On the hardware assumption.** These guides describe the *term project*, not the course. The course itself asks nothing of your hardware — it is lectures, and the demos run in class. The problem cards were sized against a single 16 GB CUDA GPU (an RTX 5070 Ti or similar), which is what a QLoRA run on a 7–8B model, or inference with a few small models, actually needs. If you have less, say so early and pick a card that fits: many of the analysis cards are inference-only, and the tokenizer cards need no GPU at all.
